title: Free and cofree evaluation for varying-site abelian sheaf systems
statement:
Let $I$ be a small category in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. For each $i$ let $\mathcal C_i$ be a small site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. For each $a:j\to i$ let $f_a:\mathcal C_j\to\mathcal C_i$ be a morphism of sites, with its additive adjunction $f_a^{-1}\dashv f_{a,*}$ and specified canonical identity and composition identifications satisfying the coherence laws. Let $\mathscr S$ be the category whose objects are families $F_i\in\operatorname{Ab}(\mathcal C_i)$ and maps $\phi_a:f_a^{-1}F_i\to F_j$ satisfying the identity and cocycle laws; morphisms $h:F\to G$ are families with $h_j\phi_a=\psi_a f_a^{-1}h_i$. For each $i$, evaluation $\operatorname{ev}_i(F)=F_i$ has additive adjoints $L_i\dashv\operatorname{ev}_i\dashv R_i$, with natural component identifications
$$ (L_iA)_j=\bigoplus_{a:j\to i}f_a^{-1}A,\qquad (R_iA)_j=\prod_{a:i\to j}f_{a,*}A.$$
Products and coproducts are in abelian sheaves, with empty ones equal to zero. For $c:k\to j$, the transition of $L_iA$ sends the $a:j\to i$ summand of $f_c^{-1}(L_iA)_j$, through the composition comparison, to the $a\circ c$ summand of $(L_iA)_k$. The transition of $R_iA$ is specified by its $b:i\to k$ projection: it is $f_c^{-1}$ of the $c\circ b$ projection, followed by the composition comparison and the counit $f_c^{-1}f_{c,*}f_{b,*}A\to f_{b,*}A$. The adjunction $\operatorname{Hom}(L_iA,F)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(A,F_i)$ is restriction to the identity summand; its inverse sends $h:A\to F_i$ to the family with $a$-summand $\phi_a f_a^{-1}h$. The adjunction $\operatorname{Hom}(F,R_iA)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(F_i,A)$ is projection to the identity factor; its inverse sends $h:F_i\to A$ to the family whose $a:i\to j$ factor is the adjunct of $h\phi_a:f_a^{-1}F_j\to A$. These formulas insert the supplied identity identifications and are natural in both arguments.

source.place: Tag 0EXZ, lemma-colim-sites-injective, arrow-indexed product construction; spaces-simplicial.tex Tag 09WG, lemma-restriction-to-components-site (5)-(7), free evaluation construction. proof.text: Construct the actual free sums and cofree products and their explicit transitions in the two supporting modules. Their named coherence theorems supply the system identity and cocycle laws and normalized generator/factor equations; the cofree theorem also gives compatibility of its explicit extension family.

Define the free functor on arrows by Sigma.map. Test compatibility on the preserved coprojections and use naturality of the inverse-image compositor. The same test, now using the cocycle of X, shows that the family with a-summand Q_a(h) followed by X.transition a is compatible.

Restriction to the identity summand and the explicit free extension are inverse. One identity follows from the system identity law and naturality of the inverse-image unitor. For the other, compatibility with a together with the normalized generator equation recovers every a-summand. These maps are natural by component composition and functoriality, giving the free adjunction.

Use the explicit cofree extension as the forward Hom map and the identity-factor restriction as its inverse. The first inverse identity is the identity-arrow adjunct normalization. For the second, the compatibility of h with a, adjunct naturality, and the normalized identity-factor equation give equality at every a-projection.

Define the cofree map on a coefficient morphism h by extending identity-factor restriction followed by h. Adjunct naturality and the normalized factor equation show its j-component is Pi.map(P_a.map h). Projections prove functoriality and both naturality laws of its Hom equivalence. Apply mkOfHomEquiv to obtain the right adjunction.

Both adjoints are additive because evaluation is additive and one adjoint in an adjunction is additive if the other is. The component isomorphisms are identities. The coprojection and projection equations of the explicit transitions and the two constructed Hom equivalences verify every normalization in AbelianEvaluationAdjoints.
